reconcile.title: Reconcile with warehouse
reconcile.intro: Enter the quantities the warehouse reports. Everything else is worked out for you.
reconcile.syncedHint: These figures were read from Fast Hub's system, not counted by hand — so this is not a physical count, and any shortfall stays marked unverified in the profit report.

reconcile.empty: No stock to reconcile in this warehouse yet.

claims.title: What the warehouse owes you
claims.intro: Returns and damage the warehouse has never confirmed receiving.
claims.empty: Nothing outstanding. Every return and damage has been confirmed.
claims.openTitle: Record something the warehouse has not confirmed

adspend.title: Advertising spend
adspend.intro: Recorded per period. Never added to product cost — it is subtracted from profit.
adspend.empty: No advertising recorded yet. Add a campaign with the button above; it is charged against real profit as a period cost — and never touches inventory cost.

profit.title: Real profit
profit.intro: What each product earned after goods, order costs, advertising and stock loss.
profit.indicativeHint: This loss came from the warehouse's own system rather than a physical count, so it may be their bookkeeping error rather than your loss.

dashboard.howTo: Nothing to enter here. Pick a period from the buttons at the top and every figure and the chart update with it.
dashboard.howItWorks: Pulls your sales, expenses, stock and account balances into one view. Profit is after cost of goods, and inventory is valued at weighted average cost — not at selling price.

products.howTo: Use Add product, then enter the Arabic and English names, the SKU and the selling price. Variants such as size or colour are added from the product's own page after you save it.
products.howItWorks: The purchase price here is only a reference. Your real cost is the average cost, which the system works out from what you actually paid on purchases. Archiving stops a product being sold and deletes no history at all.

inventory.howTo: Do not edit balances directly. Use receive, issue, adjust or transfer, so every change is recorded with its reason.
inventory.howItWorks: Every increase and decrease goes through one path that writes a movement and a balance together, so stock can never change without a trace. Balances are held per warehouse and split into available, damaged and disputed.

warehouses.howTo: Add a warehouse with its name, code and city. Exactly one is the default, and that is the one screens open on.
warehouses.howItWorks: Each warehouse keeps its own balances. A transfer runs in two steps — sent, then received — so goods are never invisible while in transit.

purchases.howTo: Create a purchase order, add the items and quantities, then add extra costs such as shipping and customs. Confirm the order, then record the receipt.
purchases.howItWorks: Extra costs are spread across the items and become part of the unit cost. That enters your average cost and cannot be undone by deleting the order — cancel it instead if you made a mistake.

suppliers.howTo: Add a supplier with a name and contact details. Payment terms are optional and appear on their purchase orders.
suppliers.howItWorks: Each supplier has a ledger combining what you received from them and what you paid, so their outstanding balance flows through to Finance and the dashboard.

sales.howTo: Create a sales order, choose a customer or leave it blank for a walk-in sale, and add the items. The order stays a draft until you confirm it.
sales.howItWorks: Confirming is what reduces stock and freezes the cost and profit at that moment. A return does not rewrite the original sale — it records a separate offsetting figure, so your history stays intact.

customers.howTo: Add a customer with a name and phone number. Tax number and address are optional.
customers.howItWorks: Each customer has a ledger combining their sales, payments and returns, so you can see what they owe you at any moment.

expenses.howTo: Choose the category and the account it was paid from, then enter the amount and date. Tax is its own field.
expenses.howItWorks: An expense reduces the account balance immediately and appears on the dashboard. Cancelling reverses the amount and keeps the record.

finance.howTo: Add your accounts, cash or bank, with their opening balance. A transfer between accounts is recorded as two legs.
finance.howItWorks: Every money movement in the app — sales, purchases, expenses — passes through these accounts, so their balances are your real cash position.

reconcile.howTo: Choose the warehouse, then enter the figure the warehouse reports for each product. If they give you two separate numbers, sellable and damaged, enter both — that is what makes the result exact.
reconcile.howItWorks: Compares your books against the warehouse's figure and splits the difference into what is confirmed back, what they still owe you, and what is unexplained loss. Only the unexplained part is taken off your stock.

claims.howTo: Use Open claim to record what you know went back or was damaged and the warehouse has not confirmed: the product, the quantity and the type.
claims.howItWorks: A claim moves that quantity into the disputed bucket — still yours and still carrying its cost, but not sellable. It then ages by the day until the warehouse confirms it during a reconciliation.

adspend.howTo: Enter the amount, the channel and the period. Leave the product blank for general advertising and it is spread across products by each one's revenue.
adspend.howItWorks: Advertising is a period cost and is never added to product cost. It is subtracted in the profit report and recalculated every time you open it, so a late invoice corrects the period instead of distorting history.

profit.howTo: Nothing to enter. Choose a period and you see each product's profit built up in stages.
profit.howItWorks: Starts from revenue, subtracts cost of goods and order costs, then advertising, then stock loss. An Estimated badge next to a loss means it came from the warehouse's system rather than a physical count.

fasthub.howTo: Copy the five values from your Fast Hub custom integration and save them here. Nothing is sent anywhere else — they are encrypted on this machine.
fasthub.howItWorks: The app asks Fast Hub what changed each time you open it, so returns and damage arrive without you typing them. Tokens expire, and this page tells you before they do.

salla.howTo: Copy the Client ID and Client secret from your app in the Salla Partners portal, save them here, then press Connect with Salla and approve the app on your store.
salla.howItWorks: Your secret is encrypted before it is stored and is never shown again. Connecting grants a token that renews itself, so you do this once and not again.

settings.howTo: Your business details, currency, language and tax number. The currency locks once you have financial activity.
settings.howItWorks: These settings govern every screen — the default tax rate, whether negative stock is allowed, and how numbers and dates are formatted.

whInvoice.howTo: Keep the Excel file Fast Hub sends with each invoice and upload it here. Read the table and the findings, copy the invoice number from their PDF, then post it.
whInvoice.howItWorks: Packaging, handling, shipping and extra-piece fees are charged to the order that caused them and come off its net profit — never off the cost of the goods, which would raise the value of every unit still on the shelf. Storage is a cost of the month, not of any order. Before any of that, each order is matched against your books and their extra-piece counts, line sums and VAT are re-derived from their own figures.

landing.heroTitle: The gap between your books and the warehouse shelf — explained, not guessed
landing.heroBody: Your goods sit in a warehouse you do not own. What comes back from customers and what breaks is not counted, so the books and the shelf disagree and the loss leaves no trace. This system measures that gap and breaks it into its causes.
landing.exampleLabel: A worked example of one reconciliation
landing.exClaims: Returns the warehouse has not confirmed
landing.exFootnote: The difference is 13 units, but 10 of them are returns you are still chasing and only 3 are a real loss. A number alone cannot be acted on; its decomposition can.
landing.f1Body: Compares your balances against what the warehouse reports and splits the difference into claims it confirms and closes, claims still outstanding, and unexplained loss booked at its own cost.
landing.f2Body: A ledger of every return, damage and shortage the warehouse has not yet acknowledged, with its quantity and its age. A claim closes when the warehouse confirms it, not when you forget it.
landing.f3Body: Profit after cost of goods and order costs, then after advertising, then after booked losses. Three levels, because profit before advertising and shrinkage is not profit.
landing.f4Body: Orders, returns and stock levels are pulled from the warehouse system on their own. A return opens a claim, and its quality check splits it into sellable and damaged.
landing.f5Body: A bundle is assembled at pick time and holds no stock of its own. Selling one removes its components at their real cost, so they never resurface as a shortfall.
landing.f6Body: Shipping, customs and handling are allocated across a shipment by weight or quantity, and the weighted average cost is updated on every receipt.
landing.f7Body: Attributed to a product or allocated by revenue, and pro-rated across the days of the period. A period cost never enters inventory value.
landing.f8Body: Every stock movement, settlement and claim carries an audit record: who did it, when, and in what quantity.
landing.s1Body: Orders, returns and warehouse balances arrive automatically, and purchases are recorded with their landed costs.
landing.s2Body: What your books say against what the warehouse says, product by product, keeping sellable and damaged apart.
landing.s3Body: The difference is attributed to a claim or booked as a loss, and lands in that product's real profit.
landing.closingBody: A private system for one store. Sign in with the owner account.
landing.footerNote: An internal system for stock, reconciliation and profitability.
landing.sourceStoreBody: Salla — orders, products, selling and cost prices.
landing.sourceWarehouseBody: Fast Hub — orders, returns and stock levels, pulled every hour without anyone asking.
landing.sourceBooksBody: Purchases, landed cost and advertising spend, entered once.

whInvoice.title: Warehouse invoices

whInvoice.unbilled: Orders in your books not billed this month
